issue_context.title: Migration script runs syntactically incorrect MySQL query
issue_context.body:
### The problem

[Migration script](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/eb3458a3d29cd3b520f489ca684bb0b83c1758e6/homeassistant/components/recorder/migration.py#L547) executes the following statement against MariaDB server which is syntactically not correct:
```
ALTER TABLE events
CONVERT TO CHARACTER SET utf8mb4
COLLATE utf8mb4_unicode_ci LOCK=EXCLUSIVE

ERROR 1064 (42000): You have an error in your SQL syntax; check the manual that corresponds to your MariaDB server version for the right syntax to use near 'LOCK=EXCLUSIVE' at line 1
```
Correct is to separate options using a comma:
```
ALTER TABLE events
CONVERT TO CHARACTER SET utf8mb4
COLLATE utf8mb4_unicode_ci, LOCK=EXCLUSIVE;
```
Introduced with [issue 56104](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/56104#issuecomment-923349327) fix ([@emontnemery](https://github.com/emontnemery), [@BudBundi](https://github.com/BudBundi))

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2022.4.1

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Core

### Integration causing the issue

recorder

### Link to integration documentation on our website

[Forum link](https://community.home-assistant.io/t/recorder-component-error-executing-query-unknown-syntax-near-lock-exclusive/412768)

review_comments:
The alter table syntax doesn't document this very well
https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/5.6/en/alter-table.html?spm=a2c4g.11186623.2.23.cb0a2867KJiYg9

But there is an example here using a comma.
https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/5.6/en/innodb-online-ddl-operations.html

```
> alter table states convert to CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_unicode_ci, LOCK=EXCLUSIVE;
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.143 sec)
Records: 0  Duplicates: 0  Warnings: 0
```

> The alter table syntax doesn't document this very well https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/5.6/en/alter-table.html?spm=a2c4g.11186623.2.23.cb0a2867KJiYg9

I agree: the statement is complicated and easy to make an error.
 
> But there is an example here using a comma. https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/5.6/en/innodb-online-ddl-operations.html

Well, the grammar reads `alter_option [, alter_option]` which means that options should be comma-separated, and then `alter_option: {  CHARACTER SET [=] charset_name COLLATE [=] collation_name |  LOCK [=] {DEFAULT | NONE | SHARED | EXCLUSIVE} }` which means that `CHARACTER SET COLLATE` is the 1st option, and `LOCK` is the 2nd.
